verdicts.note: REPRODUCED: archon 551/810 = 68.0% (523 fleet.capacity.starved + 28 dispatch.capacity_starved), architecture-docs 1,382/1,881 = 73.5% (1,067 + 315), needs_attention=true on all 551 and 1,382. At 3339b88 both capacity alerts are still emitted with needs_attention: true (with a dwell and an alert_active latch). khala retro Window lines sum to 275 wakes / 3 actions. The khala ticket had 97 attention wakes 09-25 08:28-22:03Z; the most in any 13 h window is 94, which is close to 93. #2622 and #2623 merged 2026-09-11 02:30Z. The 15-minute re-ask exists: DecisionAttention re-emits every open decision attention every 15 min and has no upper bound, although its moduledoc says 'bounded re-asks'. In the inbox each open attention topic repeats at a median gap of exactly 15.0 min. DID NOT REPRODUCE: (a) The '~18 wakes/hour' comes from the retro's own counter. In the durable khala inbox, 09-17 00:00-11:59Z has exactly 12 wakes/hour, from 3 open attentions (tickets 10, 11 and 50) at 4 per hour each. The retro counter also overstates the whole window: 275 counted, but the inbox has 195 records from 09-16 20:30Z to 09-17 12:34Z. (b) The re-ask is per open decision attention (DecisionAttention), not per paused waiting_for_human worker. The actual ticket.*.agent.attention.waiting_for_human alert fires once per episode, after 600 s, and checks AlertFeed.active_ticket_attention? first. INTERPRETATION: this is a time-window effect. The two capacity percentages come from inboxes that end 2026-09-05 (architecture-docs) and 2026-09-11 16:56Z (archon), both before or at #2622. Archon's capacity_starved stops at 09-10 23h. From 2026-09-11 02:30Z on, the four aiur-team inboxes hold 2,542 records and only 37 of them are capacity_starved (1.5%): 0 of aiur's 265 records and 37 of khala's 2,249. The present-day redundant source is the 15-minute DecisionAttention re-ask: 366 of khala's 2,249 records (16.3%) are exact 15-min repeats of an open attention topic. 'Noise sources keep changing' is supported: the source moved from capacity, to permission re-asks, to operator-decision / codex-usage-limit, to state-label-missing, to main-red. Both work items still apply to the code (capacity backpressure still carries needs_attention, and re-asks are unbounded), but the capacity item is now low-volume and the reminder rate should be 4/h per open attention, not a fixed 18/h.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Wakes that need no action dominate, but the dominant source has shifted. Before #2622 (merged 2026-09-11), capacity_starved was 68.0% of archon's inbox (551/810, 09-09 to 09-11) and 73.5% of architecture-docs' inbox (1,382/1,881, 09-03 to 09-05), all flagged needs_attention. After 09-11 it is 1.5% (37 of 2,542 records across the four aiur-team inboxes), although at 3339b88 the code still raises both capacity alerts with needs_attention: true. The current redundant source is DecisionAttention. It re-emits every open decision attention every 15 minutes, with no upper bound: 4 wakes/hour per open attention, 12/hour with 3 open attentions on khala 09-17, and 16.3% of khala's inbox in total. The separate waiting_for_human alert fires once per episode. khala's first retro counted 275 wakes and 3 actions (its counter overcounts: the inbox holds 195 records for that window). One khala ticket produced about 93-97 attention wakes in about 13.5 h on 09-25.

Read snapshot 3339b88: src/lib/aiur/orchestrator/rework_gate.ex moduledoc, and comment_wake.ex:782-880 (protect_active_comment_delivery and refuse_active_comment_rework).
verdicts.note: CONFIRMED: every cited issue and PR exists with the stated state (#2798 closed unmerged; #2817 open). The rework strand recurred on khala after the 05:57Z upgrade to 3339b88, which contains #2815. #2817 lists 5 reproductions (khala #379, #385, #392, #430, #238), and the handoff also records #420 at 13:56Z. The 08-23 quote is verbatim. NOT AS STATED: (1) The first recurrence after 05:57Z was #379 at 09:46Z, 3 h 49 m later; #392 at 11:44Z (5 h 47 m) was the third. (2) The 08-23 mechanism is the OPPOSITE failure. The agent moves the ticket to human-review, and the daemon forces it BACK TO agent:rework because reviewDecision stays CHANGES_REQUESTED (#2422: 'Completed rework cannot escape agent:rework'). It does not describe a ticket stranded in human-review. At 3339b88 the rework gate no longer routes on reviewDecision: the ReworkGate moduledoc says 'Since #2422 / #2450 ... routing on unresolved review threads, not on GitHub's sticky reviewDecision'. The 09-26 strand has a different mechanism, documented in #2815/#2817 and comment_wake.ex. A review submission is delivered once (Publisher holds it for 72 h keyed on submitted_at, and the pr_review_seen_at watermark moves past it). When the running-entry path refuses it ({:skip,_}), the ticket stays in human-review, and resume returns :inactive_state. (3) The chain mixes symptoms. Same symptom (review does not trigger rework, or the ticket is stranded): #1389/#1427, #2473/#2477, #2601/#2620, #2804, #2815, #2817, and #2798 (plain PR comments; the 09-25 00:23 strand came from the Executor using plain comments, per handoff line 158). Different symptoms: #1756/#1758 and #2422 (stuck IN rework), #2065 (over-routing todo to rework), #2801 (ci-wait release), #2337 (turnaround-time analysis). So the 'recurred after every fix' pattern holds for the strand subset: #1427 was followed by #2473, #2477 by #2601, #2620 by the 09-25/26 strands, #2804 by the pre-upgrade 09-26 strands, and #2815 by #2817. It is not a single 10-link chain. INTERPRETATION: the case for a single authoritative ticket-state model still stands, but for a different reason than the claim gives. Deriving label state from GitHub review signals has failed in both directions: a sticky aggregate (reviewDecision) over-routes to rework, and one-shot event delivery strands a ticket after any single refusal. The redesign target is to persist a pending review as durable state that is re-evaluated each cycle. It is not to remove reviewDecision re-derivation, which is already gone.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Moving a ticket to rework after a request-changes review has failed repeatedly, in two opposite directions. (a) Over-routing and loops: #1756/#1758, #2065, and #2422 (08-23: the daemon re-derived from the sticky reviewDecision and forced a completed ticket back to agent:rework; since #2422/#2450 the gate routes on unresolved review threads instead). (b) Strands, where the ticket stays in agent:human-review until a human relabels it agent:rework and resumes it: #1389/#1427 (08-09), then #2473/#2477 (09-02), then #2601/#2620 (09-11), then #2804 (09-25), then #2815 (09-26 05:30Z), then open #2817. Each shipped strand fix was followed by a new reproduction. On 09-26 the khala daemon ran 3339b88 (with #2815) from 05:57Z, and the strand recurred at least 5 times: #379 at 09:46Z (3 h 49 m later), #385, #392, #430 and #238, plus #420 in the handoff. The current strand mechanism is one-shot review delivery (a review is delivered once, so any single refusal on the running-entry path strands the ticket permanently). It is not reviewDecision re-derivation.

verdicts.note: SHAPE CONFIRMED: when a response exceeds the cap, Transport.bounded_response_collector empties the body and returns a 200. Each caller then read that as a bogus 200 failure or as :timeline_truncated, and dispatch stopped with no alert. COUNT AND ATTRIBUTION WRONG: there were at least 5 episodes, not 3. (1) #1454 (08-02 to 08-03): a 64 KiB TIMELINE cap in DispatchAuthorization halted dispatch fleet-wide on its-everdred/kevinweaver-dev. Its fix raised the timeline cap from 64 KiB to 512 KiB, as the #2816 body and the dispatch_authorization.ex comment state. #1454 is therefore its own episode; it neither caused nor fixed 08-18. (2) 08-18 on aiur: a different cap, the 64 KiB @max_issue_response_bytes on the open-issue LIST fetch (~390 KiB for 53 items). The 00:19Z handoff blamed #2139 (ci-readiness), and the 05:23Z handoff says that was wrong. Commit a506ebf9d at 04:58Z added a 1 MiB list cap. The stop lasted at least 4.6 h, consistent with ~5 h. (3) 09-03 on architecture-docs: the 1 MiB list cap (2.9 MiB across 45 issues); #2535 raised it to 16 MiB and named the overflow :response_too_large. The 9-12 h figure is confounded: the 15:49Z handoff names an SSH origin causing connectivity_lost as the root cause of the same freeze. (4) 09-20 on khala #42: the 512 KiB timeline cap (777 KB page); #2749 is still OPEN. The quote is verbatim. The 3.1 h figure is NOT supported by retained evidence: the log shows 12 deferral lines from 00:56Z to 01:07Z, #42 was relabelled todo at 00:50Z and reached human-review at 01:10Z after a local cap patch, and it had dispatched normally at 09-19 22:14Z, so the window is about 25 minutes or less. (5) About 09-25/26 on khala #257: the timeline cap again (575,125-byte page), and the ticket had to be closed and re-filed. #2816 was written for this case. CURRENT CODE (3339b88): #2816 adds a page-size ladder [50, 20] and a needs_attention alert, github.dispatch_authorization.timeline_unreadable, and the list overflow is named. Caps remain: timeline 512 KiB, single issue 64 KiB, issue_relationships GraphQL 32 KiB, open_ticket_source 4 MiB. open_ticket_source still maps an overflow to {:github_status, 200}, the same misleading shape, although it logs a warning. INTERPRETATION holds and is stronger than stated: 5 recurrences, including 2 on the same timeline path after the cap was raised once. 'Not seen after #2816' covers only about 13 h (merged 09-26 05:48Z), so it is weak evidence.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Hard response-size caps in the daemon's GitHub fetch paths stopped dispatch at least 5 times, each time in the same way: an over-cap response came back as an emptied 200 that was misread as an HTTP failure or as :timeline_truncated, and no alert fired. (1) 08-02, kevinweaver-dev, #1454: a 64 KiB timeline cap, fixed by raising it to 512 KiB. (2) 08-18, aiur: a 64 KiB open-issue list cap stopped dispatch for about 5 h (at least 4.6 h). It was first misdiagnosed as #2139 (missing ci-readiness.json) and then fixed in a506ebf9d with a 1 MiB list cap. (3) 09-03, architecture-docs: the 1 MiB list cap (#2533/#2535, raised to 16 MiB and named :response_too_large), during a freeze of roughly 9-12 h that an SSH-origin connectivity fault also contributed to. (4) 09-20, khala #42: the 512 KiB timeline cap. The daemon deferred dispatch every 60 s with no alert (#2749, still open), and the retained logs show only about 25 minutes of starvation. (5) About 09-25/26, khala #257: the timeline cap again, and #2816 then added a page-size ladder plus a timeline_unreadable needs_attention alert. Other caps remain at 3339b88, and one of them (open_ticket_source, 4 MiB) still reports an overflow as status 200.
